text:
Liam: heads-up, after the SDK 1.8.0 rollout we started seeing client-side streaming handshake failures and a spike in 5xxs from the paging path. Noticed ~10% of sessions failing within first 30s.

IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Incident opened for channel #incidents. Severity: high. Assigning on-call.

Sana: confirming. I see repeated 'handshake_timeout' and 'frame_incompat' errors in the logs for requests routed to model-variant v2-stream. Paging traffic shows elevated latency and retries.

David: @Sana can you paste the minimal repro logs? We should decide rollback vs kill-flag.

Sana: sure. logs snippet:

```
2026-03-15T10:02:12Z ERROR handshake timeout id=abc123 client=mobile-7.1 attempt=1
2026-03-15T10:02:12Z WARN kvcache miss token=xxxxx route=paging/v2
2026-03-15T10:02:13Z ERROR frame_incompat: expected=0x1a got=0x2b conn=conn-452
```

Priya: paging customers on the pogo-tier are the ones hitting it most. Ramp started at 09:45 with SDK 1.8.0 canary. Canary was supposed to be limited but routing policy allowed burst. Customer impact: increased error rates for streaming + paging calls; non-streaming text gen mostly fine.

Liam: immediate mitigation options: 1) flip feature flag sdk_streaming_v2 -> off (fast). 2) kill canary traffic routing to v2 (requires routing change). 3) full rollback of SDK 1.8.0 (client-side, slower). What's the on-call preference?

David: @Liam flip the feature flag first — we can undo quickly. If that doesn't stabilize in 5-10m, we'll roll routing back.

OpsBot: Executing feature flag change: toggling sdk_streaming_v2 -> OFF across regions (started). Command: `flagsctl set sdk_streaming_v2 false --scope=all`

Sana: applied flag in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Seeing initial drop in handshake failures. Error rate down from 9.8% to 2.1% in the last 60s.

IncidentBot: Update: mitigation applied by OpsBot. Monitoring for 15 minutes.

Priya: telling CS to hold off on broad customer notifications until we confirm stability. Messaging draft: "We're investigating intermittent streaming errors affecting some SDK 1.8.0 users; mitigation in progress; no data loss reported." Thoughts?

Liam: good. Add note that paging requests may see increased latency during mitigation window.

David: ops — can you also put a temporary routing rule to avoid sending new sessions to the v2-stream variant? If flag flip isn't fully effective for established sessions.

OpsBot: Temporary routing rule applied: route-exclude v2-stream for new sessions (started).

Sana: follow-up logs show established sessions still failing occasionally (KV cache mismatch leading to fallback). We're seeing degraded QoS but overall traffic is flowing.

Priya: I've created internal incident doc and tagged support threads for affected customers. CS will proactively reach out to top-5 accounts on pogo-tier.

Liam: TL;DR: SDK 1.8.0 introduced a streaming frame change; canary leaked more traffic than intended; feature-flag kill reduced failures significantly; routing rule prevents new sessions to v2; next steps: rollback client change or ship a compatibility shim.

David: agree. Prioritize a server-side compatibility shim that accepts both frame types while we coordinate an SDK patch. But schedule SDK rollback if shim ETA > 24 hours.

Sana: quick patch idea: accept legacy frame marker (0x1a) in v2 handler and translate to v2 frames. I'll prototype now.

Liam: handoff to afternoon on-call @David in 30m — please keep monitoring and confirm post-mitigation stability.

David: on it. Monitoring dashboards show 95th p50 token latency back to normal, 5xxs stabilized around baseline. Continuing watch.

IncidentBot: On-call handover recorded: Liam -> David at 10:32 UTC.

Priya: final note for the incident log: impacted surface = SDK streaming + paging; customer impact = transient errors and retries for subset of mobile SDK users; mitigation = feature-flag kill + routing exclusion; root cause hypothesis = client-server frame/version mismatch from SDK 1.8.0 canary.

Liam: once patch is ready, plan a coordinated SDK micro-release with strict canary caps and server-side backward compat. Add a postmortem once we verify. :white_check_mark:

Sana: prototype shim merged to staging branch. Running integration smoke now.

David: closing initial incident thread. We'll update the incident doc with timeline and link to postmortem once complete.

OpsBot: Incident status -> mitigated. Duration: ~28 minutes.

Liam: thanks team. Follow-up action items in the incident doc: review canary routing guardrails, tighten default feature-flag rollout percentages, add server-side compatibility test to CI, and customer communication template.

Priya: adding CS notes and sending targeted emails to impacted customers.

David: resolving thread here. If anything regresses, reopen and ping #incidents.

Liam: thanks :thumbsup:
